 This appeal coming on for admission this day, the court pas  ORDER Heard on the admission.
Admit.
With the consent of parties final arguments heard.

The appellant/claimant has filed this Appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 for enhancement of the compensation amount being aggrieved with the award dated 26/10/2021 passed by 24 th Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Jabalpur (M.P.) in MACC No.3724/2018, by which the learned Claims Tribunal awarded a total sum of Rs.2,89,960/-(Two Lakhs Eight Nine Thousands Nine Hundred Sixty) with interest @ 7% per annum to the appellant/claimant by way of compensation for the injuries, which he has sustained in a motor vehicle accident.

entities.text: 24 th Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Jabalpur
entities.label: DATE

sentences.text: 2. According to claimant i.e. appellant herein, the compensation awarded by the learned Claims Tribunal is on lower side and hence, need to be enhanced.

3. Since, this appeal is for the enhancement in the compensation amount awarded by the Claims Tribunal, hence the question that arises for consideration is whether any case for enhancement in compensation awarded by the learned Claims Tribunal on facts and evidence adduced, is made out and if so to what extent?
4. It is not necessary to narrate the entire facts in detail, such as how the accident occurred, who was negligent in driving the offending vehicle, who is liable for paying compensation etc.
It is for the reason that firstly all these findings are recorded in favour of appellant/claimant by the Tribunal.

Secondly, the findings though recorded in claimant's favour are not under challenge at the instance of any of the respondents such as owner/driver or insurance company either by way of filing an appeal or cross-objection.
In this view of the matter, there is no justification to burden this order by detailing facts on all these issues.

5. Learned counsel for appellant submits that in a motor accident which took place on 25/09/2018,
the appellant sustained multiple injuries including fracture of right shoulder (Ex. P/10), which is issued by Dr. Dinesh Thakur (AW 2) and accordingly to which appellant has sustained 25%

permanent disability of right hand and learned Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.2,89,960/-(Two Lakhs Eighty Nine Thounsands Nine Hundred Sixty) only breakup of which is as under :
Rs.1,20,960/- Towards loss of earning capacity including future prospect Rs.1,29,000/- Towards expenses relating to treatment Rs. 25,000/-
Towards pain and suffering Rs. 10,000/- Towards special diet, transportation etc.

Rs. 5,000/-
Towards transport, nourishing food etc.

6. Learned counsel for the appellant further submits that the Claims Tribunal has assessed the income of appellant/injured @ Rs.5,000/- (Five Thousand) per month; whereas in the year 2018 when accident took place, as per minimum wages Act it should be Rs.7,325/- (Seven Thousand Three Hundred Twenty Five) per month.

It is also submitted that learned Tribunal has awarded only Rs.5,000/- (Five Thousand) towards loss of income during treatmenet, which is on lower side and same should be awarded for three months and deserves to be enhanced.
Accordingly, it is prayed that the appeal be allowed and amount of compensation be enhanced substantially.
7. Per contra, learned counsel for respondent No.3 submits that the amount awarded by the learned Tribunal is just and proper and no case for enhancement is made out.
It is prayed that the appeal be dismissed.
8. I have heard the submissions made by learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
9. From the perusal of record, it reveals that the learned tribunal assessed the income of the appellant/claimant @ Rs.5,000/-(Five Thousand) per month.
It is undisputed that the appellant/claimant was an unskilled labourer.

The alleged incident is of the year 2018, so the income of the appellant is considered as Rs.7,325/- (Seven Thousand Three Hundred Twnety Five)
per month.

Keeping in view the law laid down by Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi & others, (2017) 16 SCC 680, 40% towards future prospects should also be added.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi & others, (2017) 16 SCC 680
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: So far as multiplier is concerned, keeping in view the law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Sarla Verma Vs. DTC, 2009 (6) SCC 121 the multiplier of 18 as applied by the learned tribunal appears to be just and proper.

10. Thus, considering the monthly income of the appellant @ Rs.7,325/- per month, 40% of the assessed income is to be added towards future loss of income, which comes to Rs.10,255/- (Ten Thousand Two Hundred Fifty Five).
So, the yearly income comes to Rs.1,23,060/- (One Lakh Twnety Three Thousand Sixty).
Learned Tribunal has assessed 8% permanent disability towards the whole body, which is found proper.
As discussed above, permanent disability of appellant/claimant is assessed as 8%.
Thus, the amount towards future loss of income after applying multiplier of 18 comes to Rs.22,15,080/- (Twenty Two Lakhs Fifteen Thousands Eighty).

As appellant has suffered 8% permanent disability with respect to the whole body, therefore, loss of income towards permanent disability comes to Rs. 1,77,206/- (One Lakh Seventy Seven Thousand Two Hundred Six).

sentences.text: From the perusal of record, it also reveals that the amount awarded i.e. Rs.5,000/-(Five Thousand) by learned Tribunal in the head of loss of income during treatment, which also appears to be on lower side, which should be assessed as three months income of appellant.
Learned Tribunal has not awarded any amount in the head of grievous injuries, which was caused to the appellant in the alleged accident.
Looking to the grievous injury caused to the appellant, in considered opinion of this Court an amount of Rs.25,000/- (Twenty Five Thousand) should be awarded.
On other heads amount awarded by the learned Tribunal appears to be just and proper, which requires no interference.

12. In view of above discussion, appellant/claimant shall be entitled for the following amount of compensation :-
 Sr.No. Head Co  1 Towards loss of earning capacity Rs.1,77,
 2 Towards pain &suffering Rs. 25,0  3

Towards medical expenses Rs.1,29,
 4 Towards loss of income for three months Rs. 21,9  5 Towards special diet, transportation etc.

Towards grievous injury Rs. 25,0  Total Rs. 3,88  Round Of Rs.3,88,
13.

Thus, appellant/claimant will be entitled for a total sum of Rs.3,88,180/- (Three Lakhs Eighty Eight Thousand One Hundred Eighty) instead of Rs.2,89,960/- (Two Lakhs Eight Nine Thousand Nine Hundred Sixty).

Thus, there shall be enhancement to the tune of Rs.98,220/- (Ninety Eight Thousand Two Hundred Twenty), which shall fetch interest @ 6% per annum from the date of filing of claim petition till the date of actual payment.
14. Enhanced amount shall be paid with interest within sixty days from the date of receipt of certified copy of this order.
Other terms and condition of the award shall remain intact.
15. With the aforesaid, appeal stands disposed of.
16. Records of the claims Tribunal be sent back alongwith the copy of this order for information and necessary compliance.
No order as to costs.

(AMAR NATH (KESHARWANI)) skt JUDGE Dinesh Thakur vs Moh. Irfan on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/153552211/
